title: First-year engineering degrees — shared electronics and discipline applications

handoff.scope: Inventory and generation/extraction requirements only. No symbol geometry, device models, footprints or application subfolder feature is implemented.
handoff.folder_semantics: folder is a proposed slash-separated logical path, not a claim of support in the current TinyCAD library browser.
handoff.source_document_base: All source_document paths are relative to the repository root, including in standalone library files.
handoff.identity: id is stable within a library; extraction may deduplicate by canonical_symbol_id, but each library is complete and permits independent duplicate assets.
handoff.pin_contract: Logical terminal numbers and signal names are not physical package pinouts. Resolve real package pins from an authoritative device reference before generating package-specific symbols.
handoff.conventions: Prefer IEC/UK teaching symbols. Power pins and polarity should remain explicit. Built-in instruments, probes, independent waveform sources and voltage-controlled sources are excluded from symbol generation. Use existing_tools configuration with the native tool defaults.
handoff.existing_tools: existing_tools and existing_tool_ids refer to supplied non-library tools, not generation requirements. Never recreate these as library symbols.
handoff.inventory_not_bom: One record per reusable symbol type, not per component instance. A bridge can be assembled from repeated diode/resistor symbols. Different resistance/capacitance values are properties, not separate symbols.
handoff.model_warning: Every record is marked not ready to simulate from this manifest. A successful extraction of artwork does not establish a valid model, mapping or instrument implementation.
handoff.optionality: experiment_symbol_ids are a coverage set of proposed implementations and comparisons, not a minimal mandatory BOM; common support symbols and explicitly optional additions are separately identified.

experiments.title: Instrument connections and measurement loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a divider's predicted output with finite-resistance voltage measurement and compare current readings with stated burden. Explain how an instrument changes the circuit.

experiments.title: DC network analysis
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a multi-branch resistor circuit and compare measured node/current values with nodal and mesh calculations.

experiments.title: Equivalent source and load
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare an original network with its port equivalent for several loads. State source resistance and avoid treating an ideal source as a complete battery model.

experiments.title: Superposition
experiments.catalogue_description: Investigate each independent source separately, then compare the total voltage/current. Show explicitly why power is not a linear sum of these separate results.

experiments.title: Electrical power budget
experiments.catalogue_description: Account for resistor, source and load power for different operating conditions. Distinguish predicted electrical dissipation from temperature rise or mechanical output.

experiments.title: RC step response
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture voltage/current, measure time constant and compare loading assumptions. Repeat with measured component values.

experiments.title: RL response and coil resistance
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare current rise for an idealised and resistive coil model. The experiment concerns its electrical terminals, not magnetic geometry or motion.

experiments.title: Damped RLC response
experiments.catalogue_description: Change resistance and compare transient oscillation/decay and frequency response. Choose sampling and run length from the expected response.

experiments.title: Impedance and phase
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare an RC/RL load's frequency-dependent current with phasor calculations. Keep phase reference and current direction explicit.

experiments.title: AC power and power factor
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare average instantaneous power with RMS-derived apparent power for a small circuit model. Complete complex-power calculations externally if necessary.

experiments.title: Passive filter and pulse distortion
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare frequency response and transient response of the same RC filter under defined source/load conditions.

experiments.title: Diode and rectifier interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Use current limiting, an identified diode model and low-voltage sine input. Compare polarity, conduction and output ripple. The rectifier topology is a proposed application of the device topic.

experiments.title: Transistor load driver
experiments.catalogue_description: Investigate drive voltage/current and output loading using a prepared transistor model. For an inductive equivalent load, compare switch-node voltage with protection included.

experiments.title: Op-amp conditioner
experiments.catalogue_description: Scale a declared low-level input to a desired output range. Compare loading, gain and saturation with a suitable amplifier model.

experiments.title: Active filter
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare the passive and buffered/active versions of a selected filter under changed loading. Use a model with adequate bandwidth.

experiments.title: Logic decision circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw a small combinational controller and verify all combinations against a stated truth table. Compatible gate models are required; programming an industrial controller is separate.

experiments.title: Sensor-to-controller interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Supply measured sensor voltages/resistances and investigate offset, loading and conditioning. Do not claim the circuit independently reproduces the physical sensing mechanism.

experiments.title: System connections and test plan
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw supplies, references, sensor connections, driver and receiving equipment, with test points. The full mechanical/process/software system remains outside TinyCAD.
